Everything checks out. Note: I did not commit these changes since committing wasn't requested and git operations go through the git skill per CLAUDE.md — leaving that for David/Master to decide.

## Report

**Task 1 — cleanup:**
- `eval-20260825T162447-6CE19C.json`, `eval-20260825T171156-9EAAWO.json` — archived to `systems/eval-harness/runs/_archived/2026-08-28-no-valid-cost-data/`. Confirmed no usable data: empty `subagents`, and the only "cost" numbers present were the fallback estimator's dummy value duplicated across every step (identical `1012683`/`155`/`0.147115` on every single step in 6CE19C — not real usage).
- `eval-20260827T162201-YWMW6Z.json` — **verified misattributed, corrected in place (kept, not archived).** Its `subagents[]` had two entries; I traced both agent_ids to their own standalone eval records. `a574875944e9402dd` (C1QQII) turned out to be Knox's plaud-ingest speaker-ID follow-up agent, not boot's own work — same bug as Task 2. `afcc425476ccb8344` (S7GYVA) is the real boot subagent ("Boot sequence complete (steps 2-12)"), and its own standalone total (7,904,697 in / 3,472 out / $2.953679) already matched its entry exactly. Removed Knox's entry, corrected the top-level totals to the real subagent's numbers, and documented both the removal and the recovery source in a new `related_records` block.

**Task 2 — root cause and fix:**

Two distinct bugs, both in the SubagentStart/SubagentStop hooks:

1. **Misattribution at link time** (`eval-agent-start.py`): a subagent got linked into "the" open turn-level record purely because it was the only one open — with no check that the spawn actually belonged to that workflow. Master's fire-and-forget sibling spawns (Knox's plaud-ingest agents, dispatched from inside boot's own turn) got swept into boot's `subagents[]` this way. Fix: when the spawn's own prompt names an explicit `workflows/{name}/workflow.md` path (already detected via `detect_spawn_workflow`) that differs from the open parent's `name`, skip linking — it's a sibling, not a child.

2. **Lost completion data at rollup time** (`eval-agent-stop.py`): the rollup wrote into "the" open turn record, re-derived at Stop time via `find_unambiguous_open_turn_record`. If the parent's own Stop hook closed it (flipped `monitoring.active`/status) before this subagent's slower SubagentStop hook ran — a real race between independent async hook processes — the record no longer counted as "open" and the write silently no-opped, permanently losing that subagent's data. This is exactly what happened to `a2d85012d16ba3d83` in UQX5N6: it finished at 16:07:48Z, ~38 seconds after the parent's Stop hook closed it at 16:07:10.7Z. Fix: added `hook_utils.find_parent_record_with_subagent(session_id, agent_id)`, which finds the parent by "does its `subagents[]` already name this agent_id," searched across open *and* closed records — removing the open/closed race entirely. `eval-agent-stop.py` now uses this instead.

**`eval-20260828T154249-UQX5N6.json` — recovered, not archived.** The real boot subagent's completion data (`a2d85012d16ba3d83`) was never actually lost — its own standalone record `eval-20260828T160250-IBQVDT.json` had the full data (2,737,846 in / 619 out / $1.149239, sonnet, completed 16:07:48Z) because that record is written independently of the parent rollup. I removed Knox's misattributed entry (`af09289d8bc5930e1`), wrote the real recovered data into `subagents[]`, and corrected the top-level totals. Second clean boot data point restored instead of an unrecoverable record.
